title: Neuropathology of Lewy body dementia: Lewy-related pathology, alpha-synuclein oligomers, and comorbid pathologies.
authors: Sekiya, Hiroaki; Matsubara, Tomoyasu; DeTure, Michael A; Dickson, Dennis W
one_liner_zh: 该文综述路易体痴呆的神经病理学，聚焦α-突触核蛋白聚集体与共病病理，不涉及蛋白质-DNA互作或AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: Lewy body dementia is the second most common form of neurodegenerative dementia, following Alzheimer's disease. This umbrella term encompasses dementia with Lewy bodies (DLB) and Parkinson's disease dementia (PDD). The distinction between these two conditions lies in the timing of the onset of cognitive impairment relative to motor symptoms. In DLB, cognitive impairment precedes or coincides with motor symptoms within the first year, whereas in PDD, cognitive decline occurs more than a year after the onset of motor symptoms. Clinically, in addition to cognitive decline, patients with Lewy body dementia have parkinsonism, visual hallucinations, and fluctuations of cognitive status. The pathological hallmark of this condition is the presence of Lewy bodies and Lewy neurites, collectively referred to as Lewy-related pathology. This is identical to Parkinson's disease, where dementia is not observed. The principal component of Lewy-related pathology is alpha-synuclein, which classifies this disorder as an alpha-synucleinopathy. While Lewy-related pathology represents a later stage of alpha-synuclein aggregation, earlier stages involve alpha-synuclein oligomers. Emerging evidence suggests alpha-synuclein oligomers may be more toxic than Lewy-related pathology. In addition to alpha-synuclein pathology, previous studies frequently observed comorbid pathological conditions, including Alzheimer's disease neuropathologic change, TAR DNA-binding protein 43 (TDP-43) pathology, and cerebral small vessel disease among others. In this review, we provide a comprehensive overview of the underlying pathologies for Lewy body dementia and their molecular mechanisms and clinical implications. We also discuss concepts including the prion-like propagation hypothesis of alpha-synuclein, alpha-synuclein strain hypothesis, and recent advances in machine learning algorithms for analyzing propagation patterns. The purpose of this manuscript is to elucidate these complex pathological conditions, advance our understanding of the disease, and improve diagnostic strategies.
abstract_zh: 路易体痴呆是继阿尔茨海默病之后第二常见的神经退行性痴呆形式。这一总称涵盖了路易体痴呆（dementia with Lewy bodies, DLB）和帕金森病痴呆（Parkinson's disease dementia, PDD）。这两种疾病之间的区别在于认知障碍发生时间相对于运动症状的先后。在DLB中，认知障碍在首年内先于或与运动症状同时出现，而在PDD中，认知衰退在运动症状出现后一年以上才发生。临床上，除了认知衰退外，路易体痴呆患者还表现出帕金森综合征、视幻觉和认知状态波动。该疾病的病理标志是路易小体和路易神经突的存在，统称为路易相关病理。这与未观察到痴呆的帕金森病相同。路易相关病理的主要成分是α-突触核蛋白，这将该疾病归类为α-突触核蛋白病。虽然路易相关病理代表α-突触核蛋白聚集的后期阶段，但早期阶段涉及α-突触核蛋白寡聚体。新兴证据表明，α-突触核蛋白寡聚体可能比路易相关病理更具毒性。除α-突触核蛋白病理外，先前研究经常观察到共病病理状况，包括阿尔茨海默病神经病理改变、TAR DNA结合蛋白43（TDP-43）病理和脑小血管疾病等。在本综述中，我们全面概述了路易体痴呆的潜在病理及其分子机制和临床意义。我们还讨论了相关概念，包括α-突触核蛋白的类朊病毒传播假说、α-突触核蛋白株假说，以及用于分析传播模式的机器学习算法的最新进展。本手稿旨在阐明这些复杂的病理状况，增进对该疾病的理解，并改进诊断策略。
